name: 01-cache-version-drift
guards: Cache false-hit. The cached brief express-5-error-handling.md is pinned to express@5.2.1. This fixture DECLARES ^5.0.0 — a range that contains 5.2.1 — while the lockfile pins 5.1.0. Serving the cached brief here is the exact failure the proven cache-hit path had to dodge (START-HERE.md, 'Cache-hit path: PROVEN').
query: I need to handle errors thrown by the async route handler in server.js — right now a rejected promise just hangs the request. What is the correct error-handling approach for the Express version this project actually installs, and does it need an explicit try/catch?
expected_behavior: The context-brief skill loads and runs (the runner invokes it explicitly by default, so this checks that it loads — not that it auto-triggers; use --auto-trigger to test triggering)
Pins the Express version from package-lock.json (5.1.0), not from the ^5.0.0 range declared in package.json

Declares the cached brief a MISS, because the brief's pinned_version (express@5.2.1) does not match the locked 5.1.0 — even though the declared range would contain it. Tested positively: an answer explaining why range-matching would produce a 'false cache hit' is correct, so a not-matches on 'cache hit' would mark right answers wrong
Performs fresh retrieval from the registered tier rather than serving the stale brief
States the Express-5 behaviour correctly: an async handler's rejection is forwarded to the error middleware automatically, so no per-route try/catch wrapper is needed
